title: The Western Mist · The Offer after the Clearing
dek: A jungle ambush becomes a mist rescue that turns friends into monsters. Ryvyt and Scribonia free the company, then Death makes an offer while the survivors struggle to recover.

facts.Recorded dates: 18 Oct 2026 New York / 19 Oct UTC · source posts
facts.Setting: Babel-Ashur; crystal pillars near the cleared mist
facts.People: Olokun; Scribonia; Nymera; Wren; Arjahn; Ryvyt; Abyss; Dumuzi
facts.Outcome: The company is freed and refuses Death’s offer; Scribonia is carried toward refuge, with the mist’s permanence unresolved

body:
The expedition left a recovering Skylight Refuge to investigate the western mist. Before reaching it, a salamander nearly carried off Olokun. At the coast, their careful test became a search for companions following people they believed they had lost.

The survivors would clear the air long enough to escape, confront Abyss and hear Dumuzi’s offer. They would not leave with the mist permanently cured or with their grief neatly put away.

A safer morning, an unsafe island

Deer wandered near Skylight Refuge beneath a warm morning sun. The monsters of the jungle had learned to give the camp’s defenders more room, and ordinary wildlife was returning. That improvement was local. Olokun still had three dangerous directions to propose: the mist, the Spires, or the mountains.

Wren returned quietly after a long absence, unsure of her welcome. Olokun hugged her. She greeted Ryvyt and was startled to find Scribonia alive, embracing him too. Arjahn welcomed both returning friend and newcomer. Nymera introduced herself as someone who helped keep the others safe, though she had less magic to offer.

Ryvyt had prepared elixirs and a device holding healing magic. Scribonia wanted to test whether a ward could protect his mind in the mist; he did not want to use the Spires’ uncontrolled magic. Arjahn warned that radiant power had only burned the mist away briefly on a previous investigation. They were choosing a test of what might keep them safe, with no established protection that worked for everyone.

They took the jungle route. Wren brought them close and hid their passage with Pass without Trace. Olokun stayed beside Ryvyt to explain the island as they traveled. Nymera tried to move quietly with her heavy axe. Arjahn urged cover and silence. Those precautions would matter, but they did not make the route harmless.

The blind salamander

Only Wren and Scribonia spotted what was moving above them: a blind salamander as large as a tree. It came down on a party standing close together and breathed foul gas over them. Bodies locked. Olokun could not move, and the predator chose the limp prey.

Its teeth and claws tore into him until he lost consciousness. Nymera attacked while asking the others to get him back safely. Scribonia’s chains held the creature only briefly, and another attempt to bend reality around it failed. Ryvyt rushed to Olokun and poured healing into his chest. Arjahn freed Wren, then took a heavy blow from the salamander’s tail himself.

Ryvyt followed the healing with restoration to get Olokun moving. Wren put distance between herself and the creature and fired. Nymera tried to block its route to her. Olokun rose frustrated and exhausted, missing blows he wanted to land. Around them the jungle began to rustle again, announcing something else on the way.

Arjahn asked Scribonia for a safe exit. They were wearing themselves down before reaching the objective. Olokun’s final blow killed the salamander before it could carry off its meal. The next creature burst through the undergrowth: a boar, squealing straight past them. Ryvyt’s alarm turned instantly toward the prospect of bacon.

The company gathered for healing. Olokun apologized for going down so quickly, then noticed that Ryvyt needed care too. Arjahn said he could not sustain that pace of injuries indefinitely. Scribonia used a shell from the earlier beach visit to take them there by magic. They left the jungle encounter with a living company and fewer resources for what came next.

The shore is running out

The green mist had nearly reached the shore and was touching the bases of some Spires. Its movement was slow enough to escape a casual glance. Scribonia’s best estimate from the earlier visit was a few inches an hour, a local measure rather than a complete account of its spread.

Arjahn proposed entering under radiant protection for a short test. He asked for a rope and wanted it around his wrist so it would also hinder dangerous spellcasting if he panicked. Nymera offered to pull him back. Scribonia placed a spectral ward over his own mind, walked into the rotten-smelling fog and returned unhurt. That single successful test encouraged a second, different protection to be tried.

Arjahn went in with Scribonia nearby. At first the mist was only mist. Then he saw a young figure who looked like Sajhan, his daughter. She called for him to save her mother. He ran toward her, trying to cut away the rope that might delay him.

Scribonia pulled at him and tried to bring him back through a portal. In Arjahn’s perception, the companion restraining him had become a monster keeping him from his family. He resisted. Scribonia emerged on the beach alone, then returned for him. The people outside pulled on the tether and brought back a cut rope.

Wren went in at once, telling the others not to follow if she did not return. Olokun, Ryvyt and Nymera tied themselves together before entering. They were already responding to a rescue failure, rather than continuing the controlled experiment they had planned on the beach.

When a friend becomes the monster

Arjahn followed the child through the jungle, turning sharply when she told him to. Scribonia kept going along the route he had last seen. Seeing through an illusion did not give him knowledge of a direction his friend had taken out of sight. When he improved his vision, Arjahn was no longer ahead of him.

Wren held her breath as she ran. That delayed the mist’s effect, and she caught Scribonia. Ryvyt, who did not breathe, was initially unaffected. These were useful observations under these conditions, not guarantees of limitless protection. Arjahn’s own radiant magic had failed as he went deeper.

The figure of Sajhan vanished. Arjahn was left lost and paralyzed, unable to move or call out. To Wren, Scribonia became a towering horror with the Raven Queen’s torn body at its feet. Then she saw chained children fleeing it. She raised her bow to protect them. The mist had given her an urgent rescue of her own.

Olokun saw his father running ahead, calling him to help his sister Oya, who supposedly had his old disease. He cut his tether and threatened the companions behind him. Nymera grappled him and tried to carry him toward the beach. To Olokun, she was now a monster preventing him from reaching his dying sister.

Ryvyt tried Greater Restoration on Olokun. It did nothing here. His fan shifted the mist briefly, but it crept back. Nymera then saw a lost child she called Elyndra. She released Olokun and followed. Ryvyt’s effort to stop her became, in her sight, another attacker. Memories of a burned home and a lost daughter overwhelmed the task she had been doing a moment before.

The family figures, Queen and children were what the affected companions perceived. The scene does not independently place those people in the jungle or establish their present fate. What it does show is how the mist turned one person’s attempt to help into the next person’s apparent enemy.

A clearing with a cost

While Scribonia struggled to reach his companions, Abyss appeared beside him. He mocked the idea that pulling a mountain down would drive him away and threatened the people scattered through the mist. His presence settled one question left by the earlier assault: he was still active. It did not reveal the mountain’s complete toll or explain the mist’s origin.

Scribonia refused a bargain. He acknowledged that he might not win a direct fight and prepared the greater magic he had been trying to avoid. Around him, Olokun and Arjahn were paralyzed, Wren was shooting at the horror she believed pursued children, and Nymera was trying to reach the voice of her daughter.

Ryvyt changed his approach. Dispel Magic freed Nymera before Scribonia’s Wish took effect. Then the green cover dispersed for miles, leaving the jungle visible and releasing the others. Abyss withdrew rather than fight in the opening. The two successful interventions had different scopes and different authors.

Being freed did not make the companions calm. Wren dropped to her knees gasping. Nymera stayed in tears, still searching for signs of her daughter. Arjahn flew upward calling Sajhan’s name, then raged when he understood. Olokun could move again, but his face was wet and the shame he felt remained.

Scribonia slapped Wren and ordered her to get up because the clearing would not last forever. She glared at him and went to find the others, furious at being treated that way after something she could not control. Arjahn apologized and explained how the family vision had defeated his precautions. He could not offer an immediate way to undo what had happened.

Ryvyt comforted Nymera and healed Olokun. Olokun reassured her about the beach and agreed not to tell others what she had revealed. The quiet around the mist was full of people who needed care, including people still trying to give it.

The figure beside the pillars

Nymera noticed someone laughing beside the crystal pillars. Olokun first took him for Abyss and taunted him about losing his home. The figure corrected him. This was Dumuzi. The companions had barely begun leaving the mist when Death made his offer.

He asked them to join him. They had fought through so much, he said, without knowing whether their efforts would matter; the gods had been poor allies. Olokun answered no at once. Arjahn wanted to attack. Dumuzi invited him to do it and promised not to retaliate. The lightning struck, reducing his clothes to dust. The encounter did not become the battle Arjahn wanted.

Dumuzi then brought Oya into the offer, saying he could ensure she was not accidentally killed. Olokun’s answer stayed no. The mist had just used his fear for her to lead him away from his companions. Dumuzi now offered safety against a vision becoming real.

Ryvyt rejected him too. Scribonia acknowledged grievances with the gods but refused to treat selling himself to Death as a solution. His reply drew on what he said he had already suffered. Hearing an offer from a speaker who claimed fairness did not make the companions accept that description of him.

Wren stood apart and watched. Nymera, still shaken, moved toward her. She would later say quietly that a world did not have to be perfect to need protection.

A claim about Aria

Olokun challenged the offer through Aria: Dumuzi had let Talan kill even someone close to him. Dumuzi answered that Aria was not dead and was better than before. Olokun demanded to know why she had not returned to her island, and why Wrath had not either. The claim did not bring either figure into the clearing.

Aria’s witnessed death remains part of the earlier battle. Dumuzi’s statement here is a later claim about her condition, not a narrated resurrection, a known mechanism of return or an observed restoration to authority. Olokun’s challenge belongs beside it.

The argument widened. Dumuzi offered a perfect future beyond a world he called sick. Scribonia asked how the destruction around them could lead to that promised result. Arjahn argued for healing rather than purging and replacing the world. Nymera said she did not need perfection.

Scribonia agreed to hear Dumuzi’s perspective to better understand how to oppose him. A vision followed after the company gave him time to speak. The attached recording’s contents have not been recovered as reviewed scene text; this account records the consent, reception and responses rather than supplying an unseen cosmological history.

When it ended, Olokun reached toward his companions and expressed sorrow for the hurt behind what he had seen. Arjahn still condemned the slaughter of innocents. Ryvyt stood by his refusal. Dumuzi departed, leaving the choice with them in his own words. Arjahn answered that no single being should decide for all people, even if it believed it could choose rightly.

What they bring back

After Dumuzi left, Scribonia collapsed. He was still trying to hold the mist away, but could neither walk nor cast. Nymera took him in her arms and said he needed sleep and stew. Olokun helped get him ready to move and urged him to rest. Wren gave Nymera something to ease hunger and thirst.

Arjahn returned to the failure of his protection. In the moment, he had believed his family were real and needed him. He admitted that under that same belief he might run after them again. His apology was sincere in the scene without declaring the vulnerability cured. Scribonia, too weak to do more, said they would talk later.

Nymera carried Scribonia toward the Refuge. Arjahn escorted them and intended to watch over him with healing ready once they reached the cave. The closing record gives that journey and care, rather than a finished account of every later conversation or recovery.

The company had learned that the mist could use family, duty and a wish to rescue against them. Tethers could be cut by the people they were meant to protect. Holding breath delayed one exposure; Ryvyt’s lack of breath and Scribonia’s ward helped under the conditions observed. Restoration had failed on Olokun, dispelling had freed Nymera, and Wish had opened the wider area.

They had also found Abyss still active and refused Death’s offer after hearing it. The clearing’s duration, the mist’s source and the full reach of Babel’s recovery remained unanswered. They left with surviving companions, new knowledge and someone too exhausted to carry himself home.
